hero.title: A channel per classroom. And one for everything else the school runs.
hero.lede: Teachers, office staff, parents, coaches and the bus company. Each conversation in the channel it belongs to, with a record of what was said and what was promised. Parents and suppliers join as guests, free, on every plan.

image.alt: The Grade 4B channel in Kolabr: the class thread with a notice about permission slips, an absence raised as a request, the parent roster on the right and the channel’s requests, events and wiki in the sidebar

channels.title: Where a school puts its channels
channels.lede: A channel is a group of people plus the work they share: the chat, the requests, the calendar and the wiki. Most schools land on something close to this.

cards.title: Grade 4B
cards.body: Two teachers, 27 parents as guests. Notices, homework, the class photo, and a private thread when it is about one child.

cards.title: Staff room
cards.body: Your own team only. Briefings, cover arrangements, the week ahead, documents nobody should see outside the school.

cards.title: Facilities and IT
cards.body: Broken projector, a door that will not lock, a login that expired. Raised as requests, owned by a name, closed with a date.

cards.title: Admissions
cards.body: Prospective parents as guests for the length of the application. Forms, interview slots, the offer, then archive it.

cards.title: Sports and extramurals
cards.body: Coaches, the fixture list, the WhatsApp-at-6am problem solved by events with reminders and a sync to parents’ calendars.

cards.title: Suppliers
cards.body: Bus company, caterer, uniform shop, maintenance contractor. Each in their own channel, each a guest, none of them seeing the others.

seatNote: Channels are unlimited on Pro and Business, and so are guests: a class of 27 parents adds nothing to the bill. You pay for your teachers and office staff, and nothing else.

parents.title: Parent communication that is not a group chat
parents.lede: Parents are guests in their child’s channel. They see that channel and nothing else, no staff room, no other family’s thread, no teacher’s personal number.

points.title: Notices go out once
points.body: An announcement reaches every parent in the class at the same time, with the letter attached. It stays on the channel, so the parent who was on a plane still finds it.

points.title: One child, one thread
points.body: Concerns about a single child belong in a private thread between that parent and the teachers, inside the same channel. Read by the people who need it, invisible to the rest.

points.title: When the teacher’s day ends, it ends
points.body: Parents raise things as requests instead of messaging at 22:40. The request has an owner and a due date, and the answer arrives inside school hours.

image.alt: Kolabr on a phone: the Grade 4B thread, a parent asking about the outing form, with the channel tabs along the bottom

requests.title: Every “can you please” gets an owner
requests.lede: Absence notes, transport changes, a projector that died before third period, a permission slip, a new login for a substitute teacher. Raised in the channel, categorised, owned by a person, closed with a date, not lost in somebody’s inbox.

image.alt: Request management in Kolabr: absences, transport changes, permission slips and facilities jobs in one table with status, priority and owner

cards.title: Your own categories
cards.body: Absence, transport, maintenance, IT, finance, permission. Each one routes to the person who actually handles it.

cards.title: A promise with a clock
cards.body: An SLA per category, so “we will come back to you” means two school days and everyone can see whether it happened.

cards.title: A message becomes a request
cards.body: A parent writes it as a message; a teacher turns that message into a request in one step and hands it to the office.

calendar.title: The term, on one calendar
calendar.lede: Parent evenings, fixtures, exams, staff briefings, the governing body meeting. Scheduled in the channel it concerns, so the people it concerns are the people who get it.

image.alt: The Kolabr calendar for a school: morning briefings, the Planetarium outing, a netball fixture and parent evening slots on one month view

cards.title: Where parents already look
cards.body: On the channel calendar, where the parents in that channel already are.

cards.title: Recurring by default
cards.body: Weekly staff briefing, Friday assembly, monthly PTA: set once for the term.

cards.title: A call when they cannot come in
cards.body: Start the video call from the event and share a screen with the report on it.

cards.title: Tied to the request
cards.body: The meeting about one child hangs off that request, with the notes afterwards.

wiki.title: The policy, written down once
lede: Uniform list, absence procedure, exam rules, the code of conduct, what a substitute needs to know about 4B. Published in the channel’s wiki, and offered to a parent as a suggestion while they are typing the question.

image.alt: The class wiki in Kolabr: the Absence and late arrivals article with its steps, reason codes and review date, beside sections for Term 3 and school routines

oversight.title: What the head of school can see
oversight.lede: Schools carry a duty of care for what is said to children and parents. Kolabr keeps that record by default instead of leaving it on staff phones.

image.alt: The channel dashboard for one class: requests raised in this channel this month, open and unassigned counts, what is due today, the people in the channel with parents counted as free guests, request volume for the fortnight, and the requests assigned to this teacher

wide.title: Every channel keeps its own score
wide.body: Open requests, what is overdue and who is waiting on the office, on the dashboard of the channel it belongs to. Admissions answers for admissions, without anyone compiling a report to find out.

deep.title: A record, not a rumour
deep.body: Every message, request and file stays with the channel. When a conversation with a family needs reviewing, it is there, with who said it and when.

cards.title: Guests see one channel
cards.body: A parent invited to 4B sees 4B. No directory of other families, no staff channels, nothing they were not asked into.

cards.title: Roles for office and staff
cards.body: Who can invite, who can close a request, who can publish a notice to every parent. Set once, applied everywhere.

cards.title: In a pocket, not a staff room
body: Teachers answer between lessons on the phone; the office works from the desk. Same channel, same record.

stages.title: Starting in September, ending in June
stages.lede: A school year is a cycle, and the tool should follow it rather than accumulate.

cards.title: Start with one class
cards.body: Pick the teacher who is drowning in messages. One channel, the parents invited, two weeks. It either helps by half-term or it does not.

cards.title: Roll over in one step
cards.body: Build next year’s classes from a channel template: categories, SLAs and the wiki already in place. Archive last year’s and keep it readable.

cards.title: You pay for staff only
body: Parents, coaches and suppliers are guests and are never billed. The plan covers your own team.

cta.title: Try it on one classroom.
cta.body: Free for one channel, no card. Seven days on Pro or Business when you want the rest. Invite one class and see what the teacher’s evenings look like afterwards.
